Australia flash PMI sinks to 46.1 as private sector shrinks at fastest pace in 5 years
articles.desc: A drop this deep, alongside the first easing in input cost inflation for months, weakens the case for further Australian monetary tightening. That leaves the Australian dollar exposed if rate markets start pricing a gentler path. The sharp fall in new export orders also points to softening external
articles.content: A drop this deep, alongside the first easing in input cost inflation for months, weakens the case for further Australian monetary tightening. That leaves the Australian dollar exposed if rate markets start pricing a gentler path. The sharp fall in new export orders also points to softening external demand, at a time when global equities are already under heavy pressure. Prices are still running above their long-run averages, though, so policymakers are unlikely to move quickly to declare inflation beaten. Traders may also treat the flash reading cautiously until the final data in early December. --- Higher interest rates are now hitting Australian demand across the board: services have joined manufacturing in contraction, new orders are at a five-year low and confidence is draining away. Summary: Australia's flash composite PMI fell to 46.1 in November from 48.2, the lowest since August 2021 and a second month in contraction. Services activity slid to 46.2 from 48.5, and the manufacturing PMI eased to 48.7 from 49.6. New orders fell at the fastest pace since August 2021, with services new business falling faster than manufacturing. Export orders fell at the sharpest rate in just over two years. Firms cut staff and cleared backlogs, and business confidence hit a three-year low. Input cost and selling price inflation both eased but remain above their long-run averages. Final data are due on 1 December for manufacturing and 3 December for services and the composite. Australia's private sector shrank at its fastest pace in more than five years in November, according to flash survey data from S&P Global, as higher interest rates and softer demand at home and abroad hit both manufacturers and service providers. The flash composite output index fell to 46.1 from 48.2 in October. That is its lowest reading since August 2021 and the second straight month below the 50 mark that separates growth from contraction. The weakness was broad. The services business activity index dropped to 46.2 from 48.5, while the manufacturing PMI slipped to 48.7 from 49.6 and the manufacturing output index fell to 45.3 from 46.2. Services output declined at the sharpest rate in 36 months, and manufacturing output at the steepest in 25 months. Weak demand was the main driver. Total new orders fell for the first time in five months and at the fastest pace since August 2021, and services new business is now shrinking faster than manufacturing orders. Firms cited subdued economic conditions, tight budgets and higher borrowing costs. New export orders also fell at the sharpest rate in just over two years, as uncertainty in overseas markets weighed on foreign demand. With less new work coming in, businesses reduced their backlogs for the first time since June and cut staff for the second time in three months. Manufacturers shed jobs faster than service firms. Business confidence fell to a three-year low. There was some relief on prices. Input cost inflation eased for the first time in four months, even with higher fuel, transport, supplier and wage costs and a further marked lengthening of manufacturers' delivery times. Firms also raised their selling prices more slowly than in October. Both measures remain above their long-run averages. Jingyi Pan, economics associate director at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said the easing in price pressures showed that the recent tightening in financial conditions was working. She cautioned, though, that falling employment and confidence point to weaker output ahead, while inflation has yet to be fully brought under control. Final November readings are due on 1 December for manufacturing and 3 December for services and the composite. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Hard Drive Prices Have More Than Doubled; These Helium Plants In The Middle East Are Part Of The Reason
articles.desc: AI data centers have driven up the price of hard drives, but there's another problem for the companies that make them: a dwindling supply of helium.
articles.content: Hard Drive Prices Have More Than Doubled; These Helium Plants In The Middle East Are Part Of The Reason Hard Drive Prices Have More Than Doubled; These Helium Plants In The Middle East Are Part Of The Reason Since 2013, helium has been encased in hard disk drives (HDDs) to provide an environment inside the HDD that allows for smoother, more efficient operation. has become a method for storage manufacturers to cram even more space onto the drives, as the low-density environment and reduced air turbulence when spinning in helium allow for thinner platters. The more platters in an HDD, the more storage can become available. However, with the rise of artificial intelligence, new-style AI data centers have hoovered up a vast majority of hardware . RAM, processors, solid-state drives (SSDs), and now HDDs have been bought en masse, causing prices to rise for consumers. Now, with the U.S. in a war with Iran, and Iran determined to undermine U.S. power, helium HDDs are being impacted even more. Iran has been striking locations in the Middle East, including plants in Qatar. Part of this strategy is to strike allies of the U.S. in an attempt to push the American occupation out of the region. Qatar also provides one-third of the world's helium supply, and its Ras Laffan Industrial City was struck by Iranian missiles in March 2026. As such, the hoarded supplies are now potentially dwindling, and so are HDDs. It's not just the U.S. and Iran — Russia and Ukraine have caused helium issues Estimates say that about one-third of global helium used to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. With the U.S. blundering its way into a war with Iran, the once freely accessible strait is now under strict controls. Some alleviation has come with the discovery of a massive deposit in the U.S. in 2024, but no plant has been constructed to take advantage of this just yet. Other locations that supplied helium also included Ukraine. Prior to the Russian invasion, noble gases like helium were produced through other manufacturing processes. Russia captured and destroyed the plant in 2022, and in 2026, also put export controls on the gas. Concerns about supplies in caverns already uncovered could add more strain, and the gas is also used in the wider chip production process, not just hard drives. Critical chips require it within the ultraviolet lithography process, draining more resources. Not all HDDs use helium, but high-end drives will. articles.title: Major Study Finds That the Internet, With All Its Intentionally Addictive Features Like Infinite Scrolling, Is Basically Cooking the Human Brain
articles.desc: A new study estimates that one-in-ten people on Earth suffer from problematic internet usage as a result of social media companies.
articles.content: Major Study Finds That the Internet, With All Its Intentionally Addictive Features Like Infinite Scrolling, Is Basically Cooking the Human Brain | United States Major Study Finds That the Internet, With All Its Intentionally Addictive Features Like Infinite Scrolling, Is Basically Cooking the Human Brain A new study estimates that one-in-ten people on Earth suffer from problematic internet usage as a result of social media companies. Doomscrolling might seem like a goofy side effect of our increasingly digitized lives, but some experts are now pegging the phenomenon as a global public health crisis.estimated that over 10 percent of the world’s population engages in problematic internet use. That phenomenon includes a laundry list of digital behaviors that have become commonplace in the 21st century: compulsive scrolling on social media, of course, but also things like problematic online gambling, compulsive spending, and excessive gaming. These behaviors each share some common characteristics, especially that they’re difficult for the affected person to control. A bigger brain doesn’t mean smarter, new bumblebee study finds As a result, the problematic internet user experiences consequences around their health, social life, education, work, and overall quality of life. “Digital technologies are now woven into almost every aspect of modern life and bring enormous benefits,” Flinders University professor of mental health and wellbeing Zsolt Demetrovics, who worked on the research,. “The challenge is finding ways to reduce harms while preserving the many benefits of being connected. ” The issue, the researchers explain, is not with the internet itself — meaning blanket bans or age-related restrictions may only work as stopgaps. Rather, it’s the host of features baked in by companies to keep users hooked and thus generate revenue via ads, clicks, and transactions. These are things like infinite scrolling feeds, targeted recommendations, incessant notifications, and autoplaying short-form videos. Elon Musk’s Full Self-Driving software, despite its name, isn’t capable of fully driving itself. But try conveying that nuance to elderly folks, who are buying Teslas with the semi-autonomous feature because they can no longer safely drive themselves. , that Tesla has been happy to play into — and represents yet another pain point as the public gets its hands on a piece of sci-fi-sounding technology. It’s an acknowledgement that they’re aging and can’t be independent like they used to be. And given the disastrous state of public transportation in this country, many can’t afford to. Without their kids to chauffeur them, how will they get around? The answer, for an increasing number, is to buy a Tesla with FSD. articles.title: Iran amasses 14 oil tankers at key export hub as Tehran weighs challenge to US blockade: report
articles.desc: Iran has amassed more than 14 tankers at its most crucial crude-oil export terminal to try to get its money-maker flowing again despite a US naval blockade, a new report said — but experts doubted …
articles.content: US Central Command Issues New Blockade Warning as Iran Amasses Tankers at Kharg Island | Politics US Central Command Issues New Blockade Warning as Iran Amasses Tankers at Kharg Island Iran has massed more than 14 tankers at Kharg Island to test the US naval blockade, while President Trump warns any convoy will end up at the bottom of the sea and experts call the plan farcical. US Central Command issued a stern maritime advisory Wednesday, warning that vessels receiving cargo at sea from ships carrying goods loaded at ian ports or coastlines could be treated as violating the US blockade, even if they are outside American forces are prepared to stop, board, divert, or capture such vessels, or order them to return their cargo to its port of origin, according to the military statement. Officials emphasized that ships refusing to comply could face further enforcement, including the use of force consistent with applicable law. Two tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as hawks press Trump to resume Iran strikes The advisory comes as Iran has amassed more than 14 tankers at Kharg Island, its most crucial crude-oil export terminal, in an apparent attempt to restart shipments despite the ongoing naval blockade. Satellite imagery and ship-tracking data confirm that crews have been assigned to the vessels and Iranian flags have been raised ahead of a possible convoy toward the Sea of Oman in the coming days. Kharg Island normally handles roughly 85 to 90 percent of Iran's crude oil exports and possesses the deep-water infrastructure required to accommodate supertankers while storing about 30 million barrels of oil. The island is particularly important because alternative export facilities, such as the port of Jask, lack the necessary infrastructure to replace it, leaving Tehran with few viable options for large-scale exports. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi acknowledged the intense pressure on the country's exports on Friday, stating that Tehran is actively pushing to resume shipments. However, the economic situation has deteriorated significantly, with shipping data showing that Iran has gone several months without significant crude loadings, as it had been loading roughly 2 million barrels daily when the war began. October marked the second consecutive month without reported loadings, according to analytics firm Kpler, signaling a severe financial blow to Tehran. In an effort to circumvent restrictions, Iran appears to be exploring alternate methods to move its oil, including conducting ship-to-ship transfers at sea to obscure the origin of the crude and evade American sanctions. Maritime security experts have largely dismissed the reported operation as propaganda, with maritime security expert Charlie Brown telling Fox News Digital on Sunday that the supposed plan by the Iranians to suddenly deploy 14 vessels to try to breach the blockade in a convoy is farcical. Brown warned that any convoy leaving Kharg Island would face the US Navy 5th and 7th Fleets as it crossed the Indian Ocean, noting that ships and aircraft are already positioned in the area. The Institute for the Study of War warned that Iran could attempt to break the blockade within days, saying that the deteriorating economic situation is increasingly dire and forcing officials to reckon with the necessity of breaking the US blockade. The think tank cautioned that such a move would risk the destruction of a tanker fleet or escalate into a larger regional conflict. Sanctioned tankers were already positioned in the Arabian Sea within about a day's sailing distance of the blockade line, and the situation has seen recent escalations, including the seizure of two foreign oil tankers in the Persian Gulf allegedly carrying smuggled fuel. articles.content: Black Friday Furniture Sale in Phoenix AZ showcases how AI Is Reshaping the Industry There were 432 press releases posted in the last 24 hours and 504,224 in the last 365 days. Black Friday Furniture Sale in Phoenix AZ showcases how AI Is Reshaping the Industry Mega Furniture Black Friday sale in Arizona through December 6, 2026 Select furniture offers from Mega Furniture’s 2026 Arizona Black Friday flyer. The Black Friday flyer lists four bonus furniture tiers. Exclusions apply. Illustration of the $1,695 and $1,995 three-room offers. See the official flyer for included items. The Sealy Posturepedic offer in the official flyer runs through Dec. 1, 2026. Terms apply. A Phoenix-area case study shows how AI search connects local furniture queries with inventory, product details, showroom access and delivery data. — Black Friday Furniture Sale Scottsdale AZ PHOENIX, AZ, UNITED STATES, November 22, 2026 / / -- Mega Furniture USA is using the 2026 holiday shopping season as a case study in how artificial intelligence, structured inventory data and local search are changing the way consumers research high-consideration purchases. The Arizona retailer’s Black Friday event runs through Dec. 6, spanning Small Business Saturday and Cyber Monday, while its longer-term technology roadmap focuses on making large furniture catalogs easier to search, compare and fulfill across 10 Phoenix-area stores. Furniture purchases create a difficult information problem for both shoppers and search systems. A sectional must fit the room, doorway and delivery path. Bedroom collections contain multiple pieces. Mattresses have different comfort and support profiles. Special orders may carry longer lead times. Current inventory, promotion eligibility, delivery timing and access to a nearby showroom can all change the best answer for a customer. That complexity is pushing furniture discovery beyond traditional category pages. A shopper may ask a search engine or AI assistant for a specific product, price range, neighborhood and deadline in one sentence. To return a useful answer, the system must understand the product request, match it to a local catalog, distinguish advertised offers from general inventory and confirm whether stock and delivery information are current. LOCAL SEARCH LANGUAGE BECOMES PRODUCT AND INVENTORY DATA High-intent searches increasingly combine a city or neighborhood with a product rather than using a broad phrase such as “furniture store.” In central and north Phoenix, examples include “Black Friday furniture sales in Phoenix,” “sectional sofa sale Phoenix,” “queen mattress and adjustable base deal Phoenix,” “furniture sale near Arcadia,” “furniture deals near Happy Valley” and “West Phoenix living room furniture sale.” East Valley shoppers may use more specific searches such as “Black Friday bedroom set sale Chandler,” “dining room furniture sale Gilbert,” “Black Friday mattress sale Mesa” or “sectional sofa sale in the East Valley.” West Valley demand can appear as “Black Friday furniture sale Peoria,” “sectional sale Glendale Arrowhead,” “furniture outlet Black Friday Glendale” and “living room set sale Avondale.” These phrases are not interchangeable. A request for a sectional in Chandler carries different dimensions, inventory and delivery questions than a bedroom set in Peoria or a mattress in Mesa. AI-assisted discovery becomes more useful when it can connect that local language to accurate product attributes, store coverage, current availability and fulfillment constraints. WHY AI SEARCH DEPENDS ON STRUCTURED RETAIL INFORMATION AI systems can interpret conversational requests, but they still depend on reliable source data. articles.title: COP31 ends without a deal: Why talks collapsed and what was left undone
articles.desc: After a record 44 hours of overtime, countries rejected the Antalya Pact draft, which did not mention fossil fuels nor a figure for adaptation finance.
articles.content: COP31 ends without a deal: Why talks collapsed and what was left undone | HT Explainers Copyright © HT Digital Streams Ltd. All rights reserved. COP31 ends without a deal: Why talks collapsed and what was left undone After a record 44 hours of overtime, countries rejected the Antalya Pact draft, which did not mention fossil fuels nor a figure for adaptation finance. ’ annual climate summit, ended without a deal in Antalya on Sunday, after the European Union, the UK and several climate-vulnerable countries rejected the final text, leaving the questions of fossil fuels and climate finance unresolved. At the closing plenary on Sunday afternoon, president Murat Kurum, who is also Turkey’s environment minister, told countries the proposed Antalya pact did not have consensus. “We recognise that there is no consensus on this document. Therefore, these decisions have not been adopted,” he said. India, speaking for the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), a negotiating bloc of developing countries, said the group had reservations about the text but remained prepared to move forward. It urged other countries to show flexibility and to uphold consensus and multilateralism. The summit had two versions of its cover decision, the headline political document that sums up what countries agree to beyond the technical decisions. One was for all parties to the 1992 UN climate convention. The other, much longer, was for parties to the and covered everything tied to Paris obligations. Both were left unadopted. COP31 becomes longest-ever UN climate summit, EU rejects 'greenwashing of fossil fuels' Decisions adopted separately still stand, including those on the Green Climate Fund, the main UN-linked fund for climate finance. The Paris Agreement and earlier COP decisions also remain in force, including the 2023 Dubai outcome known as the UAE Consensus. Everything that existed only in the Pact fell with it, including: • A new two-year work programme on mountains and glaciers • The Antalya–Addis Ababa road map on adaptation finance • A high-level dialogue on overshooting the 1.5°C limit • A report on how to measure the pledge to triple adaptation finance The summit overran its scheduled Friday close by more than 44 hours, the longest in COP history, beating the record set at COP25 in Madrid in 2019. The closest precedent for a failed outcome is Copenhagen in 2009, where countries only “took note” of the Copenhagen Accord instead of adopting it. The fossil fuel language in the first draft was dropped on November 19 and did not come back, even after two days of overtime. Developing countries came to Antalya wanting a number for adaptation finance, the money that helps them cope with climate impacts already under way, such as floods and droughts. The first draft named $120 billion a year by 2035. The second draft dropped it, and it was not added back to the text thereafter. COP31 president says climate deal ‘not approved’; EU claims oil states ‘hijacked’ talks “We didn't come here to beg,” Ghana's environment minister Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings said, according to AFP. The final draft recalled Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement, under which developed countries “shall provide financial resources” to developing ones, but did not attach any new figures to it. It repeated last year’s call to at least triple adaptation finance by 2035 without saying from what level, and asked the UNFCCC’s Standing Committee on Finance for options on a baseline in time for next year’s summit. It cited the UN Environment Programme’s estimate that developing countries need about $305 billion a year for adaptation until 2035. The draft also restated the Paris goal of aligning global finance flows with low-emission development, but no longer cited Article 2.1(c), the provision behind it. The words “fossil fuels” are nowhere in the final draft. Its opening line instead recalls the UAE Consensus “in its entirety”. That outcome of the 2023 Dubai summit was the first COP decision to

articles.desc: (MENAFN - AsiaNet News) DNI Jay Clayton Confirms Investigations into Alice Huang and MegaspeedWashington, DC [US], November 23 (ANI): Director of National Intelligence (DNI) Jay Clayton has ...
articles.content: DNI Jay Clayton Confirms Investigations Into Alice Huang And Megaspeed DNI Jay Clayton Confirms Investigations Into Alice Huang And Megaspeed DNI Jay Clayton Confirms Investigations into Alice Huang and Megaspeed Washington, DC [US], November 23 (ANI): Director of National Intelligence (DNI) Jay Clayton has confirmed that investigations into Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed, are ongoing, as the controversy surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang continues. In an interview with Fox News, Clayton said that investigations into both Alice Huang and Megaspeed were moving forward, alongside regulatory proceedings. He added that the American public would receive answers as the matter progresses. "There is an investigation into her company, and there is an investigation into her. That is going to play out. Also, I fully expect that the board of directors of Nvidia is looking into this situation. You know, that would be responsible; that's what the American people want to hear from them. And there are-are regulatory proceedings going on. The American people will get answers regarding this matter," Clayton said. Clayton also said he expected Nvidia's board of directors to examine the situation, describing such a review as a responsible step amid the ongoing developments. The controversy follows reports of an alleged relationship between former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed suspected by US intelligence agencies of having links to Chinese intelligence. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive officer on November 12, following the reports. Huang resigned following reports of an alleged relationship with a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence agencies of having links to Chinese intelligence. He also faced reports of relationships with employees at the company. Huang had acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, while Nvidia said it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets had been compromised. The controversy has continued despite the leadership transition. Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO, while board chairman Harvey Jones said on Tuesday that directors had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him. Huang had said he would be honoured to return if the board considered it in the company's interest. (ANI) provides the information “as is” without warranty of any kind. articles.title: Not The F-150: This Pickup Has The Longest Truck Bed In 2026
articles.desc: While most people might assume that the Ford F-150 pickup has the longest truck bed on the market, the truth is that it does not have the top spot.
articles.content: Not The F-150: This Pickup Has The Longest Truck Bed In 2026 Not The F-150: This Pickup Has The Longest Truck Bed In 2026 When you say you want a full-size pickup, you deserve to have that pickup be full-sized in every sense of the word. While buyers often focus mainly on towing capacity and engine output, bed length can be just as important to a truly full-size truck. Imagine you're hauling lumber, equipment, furniture, or some other oversized cargo. Engine and towing power are important to that, sure, but if you can't even fit the stuff in the truck, what's the point? That's why it's worth knowing which truck has the longest bed on the market in 2026. Right now, that's the Chevrolet Silverado 1500. Its longest available bed measures 98.2 inches, putting it far ahead of many competing full-size pickups like the Ford F-150 in terms of maximum cargo space. (The Ford truck's bed falls more than half a foot short, measuring 97.6 inches in all.) Beyond its bed, the Silverado 1500 has some other attractive credentials: Its base Work Truck trim ranks number one among 13 of the most affordable six-seat trucks in iSeeCars' , with a new-vehicle MSRP range starting as low as $36,900 (though most trims are much more expensive). The Silverado 1500's 98.2-inch maximum bed length is its standout specification, but it's not the only pickup in the GM family to have a bed of this size. Its mechanical counterpart, the GMC Sierra 1500, has the exact same maximum measurement. This is because the Sierra is built on the same underlying General Motors platform and shares many of the same important mechanical components, dimensions, and powertrain options as the Chevy Silverado 1500. In addition to their matching truck beds, both also give you four engine options to choose from: a with 310 horsepower and 430 pound-feet of torque, a 5.3-liter V8 with 355 horsepower and 383 pound-feet of torque, a 6.2-liter V8 with 420 horsepower and 460 pound-feet of torque, and a 3.0-liter Duramax turbo-diesel inline-six with 305 horsepower and 495 pound-feet of torque. Depending on the configuration, those engines are paired with eight-speed or 10-speed automatic transmissions. Their maximum towing figures are also evenly matched, with the Sierra 1500 and the Silverado 1500 at 13,300 pounds. Payload capacity is also incredibly close: the Silverado reaches approximately 2,260 pounds, while the Sierra tops out around 2,240 pounds. Even their prices are neck and neck: The Sierra 1500 has an MSRP starting at $38,300 compared to the Silverado's starting MSRP of $36,900.

articles.title: 5 iOS 27.3 changes coming to your Apple devices by 2027
articles.desc: iOS 27.3's first developer beta is out ahead of a possible December 2026 launch, and it brings with it a handful of notable changes and new features.
articles.content: 5 iOS 27.3 Changes Coming To Your Apple Devices By 2027 5 iOS 27.3 changes coming to your Apple devices by 2027 From new Siri AI tricks to interface tweaks for the iPhone Duo, here’s everything new coming with iOS 27.3. in October, which introduced several improvements to Siri AI, but the company hasn't stopped there. It has already started working on iOS 27.3, which will be the next major update for iPhone users. This upcoming version is still in beta and isn't expected to be released to the public before December, but the first developer preview gives us a good idea of what's coming next for Apple devices. The beta adds even more capabilities to Siri AI, which now integrates better with third-party apps, and also introduces a redesigned Health app. It's also the first version of the OS to enable Siri Recap on the Apple Watch. and was a huge leap forward for the virtual assistant. October's iOS 27.2 update added support for more languages, such as French, Japanese and Portuguese, and iOS 27.3 will expand Siri AI's capabilities even further. The assistant now has multiple new actions for most of Apple's first-party apps, such as Calendar, Mail, Messages, Photos and Safari. You can ask Siri to create a new playlist for you on Apple Music, schedule an iMessage for later or rotate a photo for you. The update makes Siri much more proactive, and it doesn't stop there. The biggest change in iOS 27.3 is a new API for Siri AI that helps app developers better integrate their apps with the assistant. While some apps can already interact with Siri, these interactions are mostly limited to basic commands and answering questions. Soon, Siri AI will be able to control apps using App Intents, letting you order dinner or book a table just by talking to Siri, for example. Apple says the feature is experimental and intended only for development purposes. Apps with full Siri AI support won't be allowed on the App Store until spring 2027, so you'll have to wait a bit longer to control your favorite apps with Siri. Like the iOS 27.2 update, the upcoming update also adds new languages, namely Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian. Apple teased a redesigned Health app a while ago with the iOS 27.2 beta but pulled it from the final release. Now, the redesigned Health app is back in the first iOS 27.3 beta, and it looks like Apple is ready to make it available to the public next month. The redesign divides the app into three tabs: Insights, Longevity and Browse. With Insights, Apple provides a new and easier way to understand your health data, which is especially useful for Apple Watch users. It shows your activity history, average steps, heart rate and sleep data, although it's worth noting that the tab relies on Apple Intelligence, so it only works with iPhone 15 Pro or newer. Longevity uses several metrics to give you an overview of your health, letting you know whether everything's in good shape and what to pay closer attention to, such as sleep or hearing. Apple Watch owners will also see a Health Age metric, which compares your numbers to what's typical for someone your age. The app also keeps the Browse tab with all the data available in the Health app. Safari gains Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode Safari in iOS 27.3 gets two new features that users have been asking for for years, starting with Vertical Tabs. , Safari users can now switch to a vertical tab layout instead of the traditional top bar. By default, tabs are shown as small icons, but the tab column can also show the page titles. The good news is that the new layout is optional, so if you prefer the classic tabs at the top, you can keep using it. The second new feature is Adaptive Dark Mode, and this is a big one. For years, Safari has supported dark mode on websites, which ensures the page matches the theme you're using on your device. articles.title: India Explores Space-based Drug Research With Upcoming Space Station
articles.desc: India is advancing space-based drug development, focusing on microgravity research to boost pharmaceutical innovation by 2035.
articles.content: India Explores Space-Based Drug Research with Upcoming Space Station India Explores Space-Based Drug Research with Upcoming Space Station India is advancing space-based drug development, focusing on microgravity research to boost pharmaceutical innovation by 2035. India is increasingly leveraging its space program to explore pharmaceutical innovation through microgravity research, which could aid in developing new medicines, a recent report highlighted. At the Bengaluru Tech Summit that ended November 19, experts from research, policy, and entrepreneurship sectors discussed how India's expanding space infrastructure might support advancements in biotechnology and pharmaceutical research. Known globally as the 'pharmacy of the world' for its production of affordable medicines and vaccines, India aims to merge its biopharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities with its growing space technology. Scientists point out that the microgravity environment in space, where objects experience near-weightlessness, offers unique benefits for studying protein crystals involved in drug development. On Earth, gravity influences the formation of these protein crystals, but in space, they can grow more uniformly, enabling scientists to analyze their structures with greater precision. This understanding may improve drug formulations and speed up new therapy creation. Biocon, a leading biopharmaceutical company, recognizes the potential of space research. Its Executive Chairperson, Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, noted that space technologies could alter molecular structures, fostering the development of novel molecules, intellectual property, and enhanced drug functionalities. The interest in space-based biotechnology aligns with the International Space Station's anticipated retirement around 2030, which is encouraging governments and private entities worldwide to develop commercial space laboratories. India plans to secure a role in this domain with the Bharatiya Antariksh Station, targeted for full operation by 2035. Experts at the summit's space bio symposium suggested that this station could become a center for global biotechnology and pharmaceutical research. Some scientists also argue that significant microgravity experiments can commence before the permanent orbital facility is established, allowing earlier advancements in space-based drug research. articles.title: 32 years of nominative determinism: New Scientist’s gift to the world
articles.desc: Our humorous column Feedback has been around in various incarnations for the past 70 years. While it has many claims to fame, perhaps its greatest is the ability to coin words and phrases
articles.content: 32 years of nominative determinism: New Scientist’s gift to the world | United States 32 years of nominative determinism: New Scientist’s gift to the world Our humorous column Feedback has been around in various incarnations for the past 70 years. While it has many claims to fame, perhaps its greatest is the ability to coin words and phrases That creaking sound you just heard was Feedback’s ageing joints as we painfully sat down to type out this commemorative column. We have been here for a considerable number of decades, to the point that our recollection of our earliest missives has become faded and confused. Indeed, Feedback’s history is long and storied, to the point that it would defy the efforts of even the most conscientious biographer. We have been through many incarnations, most of whom went on to do far more felicitous things with their lives. It is a little-discussed fact, one not even known to reality, that a previous Feedback helped David Foster Wallace out by composingover the course of a bank holiday weekend. Scientists report strong new evidence that specially bred mosquitoes can fend off dengue We’re told that former Feedbacks also secretly performed the guitar solos onFor these reasons, most incarnations of Feedback were and are anonymous. Indeed, the identity of the current Feedback is known only to the king, the prime minister and the head of MI5. This anonymity has its drawbacks: our collective memory only stretches back so far. Thankfully, our editor took it upon themselves to venture into thearchive, in search of the first Feedbacks. It is difficult to fully convey what the archive is like, but if you imagine the warehouse at the end ofand then insert a leaking roof and a surfeit of rats, your mental image will not be too badly astray. Escaping with only a minor amputation and an urgent need to be vaccinated, the editor delivered to us pages from the very firstThere is no Feedback, but there is a column called “It Seems to Me”, written by an anonymous person known only as “Geminus”. articles.content: UG School of Information and Communication Studies launches Industry Connect to bridge research-industry gap UG School of Information and Communication Studies launches Industry Connect to bridge research-industry gap The University of Ghana’s School of Information and Communication Studies (SICS) has launched an initiative to bridge the gap between academic research and industry practice, with a focus on making research findings more accessible and useful to professionals and businesses. , the initiative is intended to strengthen collaboration between academics and industry practitioners and encourage the application of university research in professional and business decision-making. Speaking at the launch on Friday, November 20, the Dean of the School of Information and Communication Studies, Prof. Abena Animwaa Yeboah-Banin, said the initiative was motivated by concerns that valuable academic research often failed to reach the industries and professionals it was meant to serve. She said although academics conducted research and published their findings in scholarly journals, industry practitioners often did not engage with those publications, limiting the practical impact of the research. “When we do the research, we publish in academic journals, we get promoted, but the real value of the research, which is the findings and how they can shape decisions in the world, that value is missed out on us because industry people are not reading academic journals,” she said. Prof. Yeboah-Banin said the initiative sought to shift the emphasis from academic publication alone to ensuring that research findings translated into practical benefits for society and informed decisions across industries. She said her experience working in the advertising industry while maintaining an academic role had exposed her to situations where professionals needed evidence-based information to guide decisions but lacked the resources or opportunity to conduct fresh research. According to her, many challenges confronting professionals in their respective fields could be addressed through research already undertaken in universities, if stronger channels existed to make those findings accessible. She stressed that the challenge was not limited to communication professionals but extended to practitioners across disciplines and sectors who needed reliable evidence to guide their work. Prof. Yeboah-Banin said the School’s focus on information and communication placed it in a position to strengthen the relationship between academic research and the industries that could benefit from it. She added that Industry Connect formed part of her vision when she applied for the position of Dean, with Friday’s launch marking the beginning of efforts to realise that vision. “Today we set the ball rolling for bringing that vision to life,” she said.
